title: Regional Affairs Officer-Middle East (I) (Gen to 2ndLt) FMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
5. MOS 8224, Regional Affairs Officer-Middle East (I) (Gen to 2ndLt) FMOS,
DC PP&O

    a. Summary. Regional Affairs Officers (RAO)s are officers who have
completed extensive graduate-level study of international relations, with an
emphasis in regional studies appropriate to a designated region, and/or have
extensive in-country pol-mil experience in a designated region. RAOs lack
proficiency in regional language and therefore do not qualify as a Foreign
Area Officer (FAO). This FMOS will be assigned and voided only by the
authority of CMC (MM). This FMOS will be automatically voided on assignment
of the FAO FMOS for the designated region.

    b. Prerequisites. Must have either graduate work in international
relations/regional affairs for the designated region, extensive politico-
military experience in the region, or a combination of both.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Security requirement: TS/SCI security clearance eligibility
based on a tier 5 background investigation.

        (2) Display extensive knowledge of a designated region to include
military forces, culture, history, sociology, economics, politics, and
geography.




                                         1-332                   Enclosure (1)
 1145                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



    d. Duties. Uses the knowledge of military forces, culture, history,
sociology, economics, politics, and geography of selected areas of the world
to perform duties as directed. Performs in operational and strategic level
Marine Corps, joint, or combined staffs in operations, planning, security
cooperation, or intelligence billets; or within the Defense Attaché System
(DAS).

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Political Scientists 19-3094.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
